scale.note: Mode count on a fixed field scales as (100/242)^2. The Holocene node has no later chronospecies, so the wavelength is held at this detail scale.

equations.activator: du/dtau = D_u laplacian(u) + (a - u + u^2 v)
equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = larger eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(D_u, D_v)
equations.selected_wavenumber: k_c = argmax_k sigma(k), lambda_c = 2 pi / k_c
equations.onset_shortcut: k_onset^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v), equal to k_c only on the Turing threshold

law.boundary_conditions: periodic on a rectangular primordium patch (classical Turing setting)

what_changes_at_this_scale.versus_tier_center_100_um: Selected wavelength lengthens 2.42x and wavenumber falls by the same factor. Spot count on a fixed anatomical field falls to (100/242)^2 of the tier-center count.
what_changes_at_this_scale.versus_predecessor: No predecessor chronospecies is in the Gekko series.
what_changes_at_this_scale.versus_successor: No successor. The extant Holocene terminal does not shift lambda further.

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) gives the dispersion relation whose fastest mode selects a wavelength.
Murray (1981) uses that wavelength as a pre-pattern for animal coat markings.
Manukyan et al. (2017) and Fofonjka & Milinkovitch (2021) show reptile skin can realize a mesoscopic reaction-diffusion pattern, in Timon rather than Gekko.
Saenko et al. (2013) show gekkotan color is a colocalization of structural and pigmentary cells, in Phelsuma rather than Gekko.
The 242 um figure is this slot's primordium detail scale, not a caliper reading from the unscaled Dupont photograph.
